summary.intent: Get the sweep findings (trails #201-#211) fixed across stacked branches, then diagnose and fix the widespread CI failures that appeared once PRs were opened.
summary.outcome: The four #211 Rust branches were reported pushed and linked. CI turned out to be failing on about eight PRs (mostly Lint: cargo fmt, oxfmt, oxlint, a typo), and a fixer worker was dispatched to run the full lint gate on each and push plain commits. A memory rule was saved to require the full gate from workers.

repo: The repo's full lint gate is `just lint doc-check machete typos`; CI's Lint job fails if any part fails, and the `CI` job is only an aggregate that goes red when Lint does.

Lint failures seen: `cargo fmt --check` on test code (#335, #343, #345, #348), `oxfmt --check` (#332, #344 markdown), oxlint wanting `Array#toSorted()` in `preset.test.ts` (#344), and a typo `nver` for `never` (#353).
The 'Entire Gates' check is an agent-review check, so failures there are real review comments rather than formatting.
Worktrees produce 9 known core test failures from snapshot artifacts and can leave `*.snap.new` files that get committed accidentally.
Config tests need `tsx`, and in a worktree it can be symlinked from the main checkout's `node_modules`.
In the sandbox, 14 `watch_process` and `commands` tests fail because a pty is denied; all 144 pass unsandboxed.
Bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (28 to 29) regenerates the golden snapshot and will conflict with other branches that regenerate it, e.g. `feat/enum-props`.

code.finding: The disconnect arm now adds a Warning diagnostic on the component when the TypeScript checker drops its sender without answering; structural props are kept.
A `spawn_demand` helper contains panics for both top-level and nested dependency demands, so a nested panic no longer escapes the rayon scope.
Carries the new `CollectedObjectField.tags` into props so inline object-literal props keep JSDoc tags such as `@deprecated`.

workflow: Workers must run the repo's full lint gate before pushing, and CI status should be checked before declaring work done; this was saved as a memory rule.
Accidentally committed files should be removed with follow-up commits rather than force-push; squash on merge hides the bad commits.
Stacked branches must be merged bottom-up and wait for their base.
Reproducing each fix with a failing exact-content test first worked well for the workers.

friction: Workers pushed branches that failed CI because only targeted tests, clippy and sometimes the formatter were run, not the full lint gate.
The first log grep for CI failures only caught noise, and the cause of the #362 Lint failure was still not found.
Two `*.snap.new` commits (ce8ebd7d, db17d27a) were accidentally pushed and remain in history.
Work was reported as done before CI had run on it, which the user called out.
open_items: Wait for the fixer worker to finish all eight Lint-failing PRs, then verify CI goes green.
Find why #362 Lint fails, and why #324 fails (likely unrelated and not to be fixed by this work).
Triage the real review findings behind the red 'Entire Gates' check on about ten PRs once Lint is green.
The collapsed 'notable props' path (`collapsed_source`) still drops tags for inline fields.
Start trail #210 (history-comment and dead-code cleanup) only when the user says so, cut from fresh main after the rest merges.
Decide on the hand-made 0.9.0 GitHub Release; `docs/release-0-9-0` waits on it.

Run the oracle on antd and shadcn for the type and component-drop fixes, and watch the first CI runs for the Linux x64 glibc build, Linux NAPI tests, hand-edited snapshots and Storybook provider tests.
Remove the read-only sweep checkout at `/tmp/claude-501/sweep/wt` if wanted.
Long-tail low-severity findings and two watch gaps (symlinked workspace edits, tsconfig `extends` edits) are deliberately left documented but unfixed.
